meta.title: Synap Mentor — Mobile App Maintenance Mode & Version Update APIs
meta.scope: iOS and Android apps only. A request counts as a mobile-app request when its X-App-Platform header is 'ios' or 'android' (case-insensitive). Requests with X-App-Platform 'web', or with no X-App-Platform, are never blocked by maintenance mode, so the web apps and their APIs behave exactly as before.
meta.verified: All endpoints and every error path below were called against the running API on 2026-10-24, with both platforms. The example bodies are the real responses from those calls. IDs, timestamps and request_id values come from that test run and will differ in your environment. The store URLs are placeholders.
meta.verified_event_artwork: The two community-event artwork endpoints (solver-upload-event-poster, solver-upload-event-cover) were added on 2026-10-24. Called live with X-App-Platform android and no token: both return 401 'Authentication required', which confirms the routes are registered and reachable from the app. Every other error body and the success shape are traced from the handler and service code, not called live: a successful call replaces a real event's artwork and deletes the old file from R2. The upload itself was exercised from the SolverUI, and the resulting R2 objects (image/png, with event metadata) were confirmed in the bucket.

client_headers.X-App-Platform: ios | android. Mobile apps must send it on every request. It also identifies the request as mobile for maintenance mode.
client_headers.X-App-Version: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH of the installed app, e.g. 1.4.2. The existing ClientContextMiddleware validates it on every request and returns 400 if it is malformed.

response_envelope.code: string (machine-readable error code, where one is listed)

common.version_format: Strict MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, three unsigned integers of 1-6 digits each. Rejected: '1.2', '1.2.3.4', 'v1.2.3', '-1.2.3', '+1.2.3', '1.2.3-beta', '1.2.3+45'. Parts are compared as numbers, so 1.10.0 is newer than 1.4.0. Leading zeros are normalised in responses ('01.2.3' becomes '1.2.3').
common.admin_auth: The admin endpoints sit in the /api/v1/admin group, which runs AuthMiddleware and then RequireRole('admin'). The admin panel authenticates with the PASETO access_token cookie from POST /api/v1/auth/admin/login. Because the session is cookie-based, a POST also needs the X-CSRF-Token header, set to the value of the csrf_token cookie.
common.rate_limits: The public endpoints are covered by the /public group limiter, RateLimitGlobal(RATE_LIMIT_GLOBAL_PER_HOUR, default 1000/hour per IP). The admin endpoints are covered by the global stack only.
common.caching: The maintenance state is cached in memory for 10 seconds, and release info for 30 seconds. An admin change applies immediately on the instance that handled it. Other instances pick it up within the cache window.

maintenance_mode_behaviour.when_enabled: Every mobile-app request (X-App-Platform ios/android) gets HTTP 503, with the admin's message, as long as its path is not on the exempt list below. This includes login, refresh, all seeker/solver APIs, the public APIs and the WebSocket upgrade.
exempt_paths: /api/v1/public/app/*  (maintenance status + version check, so the app can still show the message and a forced update)
/api/v1/admin, /api/v1/admin/*  (admin APIs; these still require an admin session)
maintenance_mode_behaviour.never_affected: Requests with X-App-Platform 'web' or with no X-App-Platform: the SeekerUI, SolverUI, AdminUI and LandingPage web apps, webhooks, and server-to-server calls.

Scheduled upgrade in progress.
Back by 02:00 UTC.

data.message:
Scheduled upgrade in progress.
Back by 02:00 UTC.

recommended_client_flow: 1. At launch, call GET /api/v1/public/app/version-check. If update_type is 'mandatory', show a blocking update screen that links to download_url. If it is 'optional', show a dismissible prompt.
2. Call GET /api/v1/public/app/maintenance. If maintenance_enabled is true, show the message on a full-screen maintenance view and poll this endpoint (for example every 60 s) until it returns false.
3. Treat any API response with HTTP 503 and code MAINTENANCE_MODE as a switch to the maintenance view, using data.message. This covers maintenance that starts while the app is open.

endpoints.summary: Compares the installed app version with the platform's release info, and returns whether an update is available, whether it is mandatory, and where to download it.

query_params.name: platform
query_params.required: yes; falls back to the X-App-Platform header if omitted

query_params.name: version
query_params.required: yes; falls back to the X-App-Version header if omitted

decision_rules: installed < latest_version and the release is_mandatory → 'mandatory'

response_fields.update_available: boolean. True whenever update_type is not 'none'.
response_fields.is_mandatory: boolean. True when THIS install must update before it can be used.
response_fields.download_url: string. App Store / Play Store URL; empty until an admin sets it.

endpoints.summary: Uploads (or replaces) a community event's POSTER: the portrait flyer shown in full beside the event details. Only the owner of the hosting community can call it, and only while the event is upcoming or ongoing. Uploading artwork does NOT use up the host's one-time event edit. A replaced poster is deleted from storage.

auth.note: Mobile apps send Authorization: Bearer <access_token> with X-App-Platform ios/android and no auth cookies; CSRF is skipped in that case. Ownership of the event's community is checked in the service, not by the role.

path_params.name: event_id
path_params.type: string UUID of the community event

body.file: binary (required, multipart field name 'file'). JPG, PNG, WebP or GIF, at most 5 MB (5242880 bytes). The type is detected from the file's bytes; the filename and the part's Content-Type are ignored, so SVG or a renamed file is rejected.

request.recommended_size: Portrait, e.g. 1080×1350 (4:5). It is displayed uncropped.

checks_in_order: 5. File bytes are JPG / PNG / WebP / GIF (400)
7. Event belongs to a community (platform-wide events are admin-managed) and the caller owns that community (403; 404 if the community is gone)
8. The community is active, not archived or admin-locked (403)
9. The event is upcoming or ongoing, not completed or cancelled (409)

response_fields.poster_url: string. A signed R2 URL for the new poster, valid for 10 minutes. Show it straight away, but do not store it: re-read the event to get a fresh URL.

endpoints.read_side: After upload, the poster appears as poster_url on GET /api/v1/events, GET /api/v1/events/:event_id and GET /api/v1/events/calendar (omitted when the event has no poster). Each read returns a fresh signed URL valid for 10 minutes. The stored value is the R2 key communities/<community_id>/events/<event_id>/poster/<timestamp>-poster.<ext>.

endpoints.summary: Uploads (or replaces) a community event's COVER: the wide banner shown across the top of event cards (cards fall back to the poster when there is no cover). The details view shows the poster only, never the cover. Same rules as the poster endpoint: owner of the hosting community only, while the event is upcoming or ongoing, does not use up the one-time event edit, and a replaced cover is deleted from storage.

path_params.name: event_id
path_params.type: string UUID of the community event

body.file: binary (required, multipart field name 'file'). JPG, PNG, WebP or GIF, at most 5 MB (5242880 bytes). Type detected from the file's bytes, as for the poster.

request.recommended_size: Wide, e.g. 1600×700. Cards show it at 16:7, cropped to fill.

response_fields.cover_image_url: string. A signed R2 URL for the new cover, valid for 10 minutes. Do not store it; re-read the event for a fresh URL.

endpoints.read_side: After upload, the cover appears as cover_image_url on GET /api/v1/events, GET /api/v1/events/:event_id and GET /api/v1/events/calendar (omitted when the event has no cover). The stored value is the R2 key communities/<community_id>/events/<event_id>/cover/<timestamp>-cover.<ext>.
